claims.confidence: preliminary inference from public regulator criteria
claims.statement: FDA and EMA materials expose a public fit-for-purpose assessment frame that can seed a versioned, vendor-neutral review workflow. The founder could own its implementation and decision rubric without collecting participant data, but no evidence shows that sponsors will accept this founder as an independent reviewer.

claims.confidence: evidence for the decision requirements; preliminary for this offer
claims.statement: A sponsor choosing a wearable-derived trial measure must address verification, validation, usability, participant suitability, data integrity, and meaningful interpretation. The proposed paid event is the go-no-go decision before protocol lock, but the cost and deadline of that decision remain sponsor-specific.

claims.confidence: category evidence with candidate-specific procurement unknown
claims.statement: Peer-reviewed category economics show that useful digital endpoints can create material sponsor value and that established digital-measure agreements can command substantial budgets. This supports a sponsor budget class but does not establish a diligence fee, procurement access, or willingness to buy from a new Warsaw operator.

claims.confidence: evidence for substitutes; differentiation is an unvalidated hypothesis
claims.statement: Clario and Koneksa already combine endpoint science, validated measures, regulatory-grade infrastructure, analytics, and sponsor relationships, while Samsung and Alcedis show device-maker and CRO bundling. The redesign differentiates through buyer-side vendor neutrality, but public evidence does not establish that this positioning is protected or preferred.

Observed uptake of newer digital health technologies in sponsored trials has been tepid and biased toward conventional devices, so regulator-defined diligence need does not imply broad urgency or repeat demand for this assurance offer.

claims.confidence: evidence for avoided study burden; economics remain a hypothesis
claims.statement: Novel endpoint validation can be costly, multidisciplinary, and require multiple prospective studies. Restricting the offer to pre-study evidence diligence avoids self-funding those studies, but the resulting delivery cost, expert-review burden, liability, and gross margin have not been validated.

contrary_evidence: Clario and Koneksa already sell overlapping endpoint science, validated measures, platforms, and regulatory-grade services with established sponsor relationships.
Samsung's partnership with Alcedis shows device makers and CROs can bundle wearable hardware, biomarker expertise, and clinical-research infrastructure around the same decision problem.
A 2024 sponsored-trial analysis found tepid adoption of newer digital health technologies, weakening any assumption of broad or urgent demand.
No evidence establishes that sponsors will pay a separate independent adviser rather than use internal experts, a CRO, the device vendor, or an established endpoint platform.
A public-criteria review workflow is more obtainable than a consented cohort but may also be easier for incumbents and other consultants to copy.

economics.acquisition_route: Choose one disease-specific exploratory or secondary endpoint decision, seek a prepaid design-partner audit through independent biostatistician, regulatory-adviser, and investigator referrals, and do not hire or build a platform before a buyer exposes a real dossier, deadline, and budget.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A base case of bespoke diligence may remain a small consultancy and may not meet the founder objective. A credible path requires repeated sponsor programs, hired reviewers, and a subscription workflow that standardizes evidence intake, change-control monitoring, and portfolio review without claiming client-confidential data as a moat; none of that repeat demand is yet proven.
economics.founder_time: Target 10-15 founder hours per week for evidence mapping, quantitative analysis, and client decisions, with qualified specialist review contracted per engagement; this workload assumption requires a paid-pilot time log.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Revenue is the fixed diligence fee; direct costs are contracted regulatory, clinical, or biostatistical review, professional insurance allocated to the engagement, and software. Margin must be measured from a paid pilot rather than inferred from established-vendor contract values.
economics.payback: Require an upfront milestone that covers all subcontracted specialist review; recover the reusable rubric and workflow setup within the first two paid sprints only if actual delivery hours and expert costs support it.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated pilot hypothesis: a fixed fee for one endpoint go-no-go sprint with explicit scope and a paid change order for additional vendor or protocol analysis; offer a portfolio retainer only after a client demonstrates repeat protocol-review demand.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeat is tied to each new protocol, endpoint, device, vendor, population, or material algorithm change; a retainer is justified only if one sponsor has a recurring program rather than a single decision.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A versioned sponsor-side evidence rubric, cross-vendor change-control checklist, reusable quantitative review software, and non-confidential failure-mode library rather than participant-data ownership
fingerprint.customer: Small and mid-sized biotech clinical-development teams considering a wearable-derived secondary or exploratory endpoint without a dedicated internal digital-measures group
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Targeted referrals from independent biostatisticians, regulatory advisers, and disease-specific investigators plus trigger-based outreach around announced trial planning; the first credible procurement route remains unvalidated
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A two-to-four-week fixed-scope independent endpoint assurance sprint, followed only after demonstrated repeat demand by a portfolio retainer for recurring protocol and vendor reviews; the company does not operate participant studies or license cohort data
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A clinical-development, biomarker, or digital-health lead pays a fixed diligence fee at the endpoint go-no-go and vendor-selection decision before participant recruitment
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Before protocol lock, a team must decide whether a proposed device and measure are fit for the intended context or should be rejected, renegotiated, or given a narrower validation plan before expensive study commitments

founder_fit: The founder's neuroscience, biosignal, statistics, data-science, and AI experience fits evidence mapping, quantitative review, and workflow automation.

Removing participant recruitment and study operations makes a tightly scoped prepaid sprint more compatible with the founder's five-hour-per-day ceiling and preference for analytical, low-camera work.
Contracting specialist regulatory or clinical review per engagement keeps fixed capital below the original study-operator model, while preserving a test-before-scale path.

redesign.economic_effect: The redesign removes cohort recruitment, participant compensation, ethics and physician-led study operations, consent and recontact governance, and cross-sponsor data-licensing rights from the initial offer. It lowers modeled starting capital from 40000 PLN to 12000 PLN, replaces study fees plus pass-through costs and speculative dataset licensing with fixed-scope diligence and only evidence-triggered retainers, and reduces founder operations toward analysis. It gives up the presumed cohort-data moat and leaves sponsor access, credibility, specialist-review cost, liability, pricing, and repeat demand explicitly unproven.

risks: Sponsors may prefer an incumbent platform, CRO, device vendor, or internal digital-measures team and decline a separate buyer-side assurance purchase.
Incomplete or vendor-controlled evidence can make a fixed-scope review inconclusive and expose the business to scope, liability, and reputation risk.
The workflow and public evidence base may be copied unless repeated engagements produce genuinely better non-confidential decision tooling.
Portfolio-retainer and software leverage may not emerge, leaving a specialist consultancy with an uncertain path to the founder's net-worth objective.

structure.commercial_archetype: Productized buyer-side technical and regulatory diligence with a possible portfolio-retainer extension
structure.control_point: The vendor-neutral evidence decision workflow and sponsor-facing go-no-go dossier used before protocol lock
structure.critical_dependency: Access to adequate sponsor and vendor evidence dossiers plus buyer willingness to procure independent assurance before protocol lock

thesis: Replace the capital- and rights-intensive micro-study foundry with a sponsor-side, vendor-neutral endpoint go/no-go assurance sprint before protocol lock. The business uses public regulator criteria and buyer- or vendor-furnished evidence to produce a context-of-use definition, evidence-gap map, quantitative validation plan, device change-control requirements, total-cost scenarios, and procurement acceptance criteria. It owns the review workflow and decision deliverable rather than participants, devices, clinical infrastructure, or cross-sponsor health data.
title: Independent Digital Endpoint Assurance
uncertainties: Which single disease, endpoint concept, sponsor decision deadline, and endpoint hierarchy produce an urgent first assurance engagement.
Whether a sponsor will share adequate device, algorithm, validation, and protocol materials with a new independent reviewer before procurement.
Acceptable vendor credentials, sponsor procurement cycle, first-engagement price, sales conversion, CAC, and whether independent review is a line item or must be embedded in a broader CRO contract.
The legal and professional boundary between evidence diligence and regulated medical, statistical, or regulatory advice, including insurance and specialist sign-off requirements.
Delivery hours, subcontracted expert cost, achievable gross margin, repeat frequency across sponsor programs, and willingness to buy a portfolio retainer.
Whether non-confidential decision patterns and review software compound enough to create durability without cross-sponsor participant data or exclusive vendor evidence.
Whether the founder can build sponsor trust and manage diligence engagements within five hours per day while retaining full-time employment.
